description: Ex-Saudia L-1011-200 TriStar c/n 1190, delivered to Saudia 23 Sep 1980 (aerialvisuals). Displayed in full Saudia livery on the forecourt outside the museum as its landmark gate guard. Photographed ABPic 25 Apr 2012, Commons 2008 and 2012, reported by visitors May 2022 (allplane.tv) and 2024 (theotherpaths). Coordinates of airframe 24.75445 46.74055 (aerialvisuals).
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: Boeing 707-368C c/n 21081, delivered to Saudia 25 Sep 1975 as HZ-HM1, then Saudi Royal Flight / government VIP aircraft as HZ-HM2 from Aug 1979 to Aug 2003, to the museum 2003 (aerialvisuals). Outdoor, Saudia livery, has a boarding staircase. Photographed ABPic Apr 2012 (which gives c/n as 20181, probably a typo), Commons Dec 2009, seen by visitors 2022 and 2024.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: RSAF C-130H 460 c/n 4566, built 1974, damaged beyond repair on the ground at Jeddah in Nov 1989 and later moved to the museum (aerialvisuals). Outdoor static park. Photographed ABPic 27 Apr 2012, Commons 2008 and 2013, seen 2022 and 2024 and a Jan 2026 visitor review names the C-130 as a highlight.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: Second two-seat F-15 prototype (TF-15A / F-15B 71-0291, c/n 12/B002), later the McDonnell Douglas Strike Eagle demonstrator, retired to battle-damage-repair training at Robins AFB and then transferred to Saudi Arabia for display in RSAF colours (aerialvisuals dossier; thisdayinaviation.com). Displayed outdoors as an RSAF F-15; the RSAF-style serial painted on it has not been read from a photo (aviationmuseum.eu lists it as 1315, unverified). Photographed Commons 2008, seen 2022 and 2024.
aliases: F15; F15B; TF-15A; Strike Eagle demonstrator; 1315; TF15A
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: RSAF Tornado ADV (F.3) 2915, c/n 773/DS009/3359 (aerialvisuals). Outdoor static park at 24.75374 46.73751. Photographed Commons 2008, airhistory.net photo 901339, seen by visitors 2022 and 2024.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: Ex-RAF Lightning F.2 XN770, supplied to the RSAF under Magic Carpet in 1966 as 52-656, later re-serialled 52-610 (thunder-and-lightnings.co.uk, Lightning Association). Painted simply 610. Indoor hall. Photographed ABPic 27 Apr 2012.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: RSAF Lightning T.55 55-716 (thunder-and-lightnings.co.uk and Wikipedia survivor lists), painted with code 230. Photographed ABPic 27 Apr 2012 and Commons Dec 2009; listed indoors by aerialvisuals. Note aviationmuseum.eu also lists a Lightning T.4 54-608 here, which is the airframe actually displayed at Prince Sultan Air Base, Al Kharj, and is not repeated here.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: Ex-RAF Hunter F.6A XJ634, c/n 41H/688051, displayed in RSAF markings as 60-602 (ABPic 27 Apr 2012; aerialvisuals photo Mar 2014). The RSAF received six ex-RAF Hunters under Magic Carpet in 1966; whether this airframe actually served in Saudi Arabia is not established by the sources. aviationmuseum.eu also lists a second Hunter marked 60-604 described as a replica; not confirmed.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: RSAF Vampire FB.52 504 (ABPic 27 Apr 2012, aerialvisuals). aviationmuseum.eu lists two Vampires here (504 or 228, and 541); only 504 is photographically confirmed.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: RSAF Chipmunk 600, c/n C1-1003 (aerialvisuals). Indoor display halls. Listed by aviationmuseum.eu and aerialvisuals; Wikipedia lists a Chipmunk Mk 10.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: Built as A-26C-25-DT 43-22679, c/n 18826, converted to B-26B, delivered to the RSAF 18 Feb 1954 as 302 (aerialvisuals). Photographed ABPic 27 Apr 2012 painted 302 and Commons Dec 2009. aviationmuseum.eu lists it as 612 and a 2019 blog calls it TA-26B 301; painted marking 302 is used here. Outdoor at 24.75357 46.73739.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: C-47B-28-DK 44-76318, c/n 15902/32650, presented by President Roosevelt to King Abdulaziz after their Feb 1945 meeting and registered HZ-AAX; regarded as the founding aircraft of Saudi Arabian Airlines and of Saudi aviation (aerialvisuals; ABPic 26 Apr 2012; Saudipedia). Indoor hall. Has also carried the marking HZ-SA-R-1 / HZ-SAR1 on display (aviationmuseum.eu, aerialvisuals).
aliases: DC-3; DC3; C47B; 44-76318; 15902; HZ-SA-R-1; HZ-SAR1; Roosevelt Dakota; C47
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: C-54A-5-DC 42-72198, c/n 10303, ex N88782 and N68961 (Transocean), then HZ-AAH and RSAF 450 (aerialvisuals). Found derelict at old Jeddah Kandara airport after 1981 and moved to Riyadh. Outdoor at 24.75444 46.73860. Photographed ABPic 27 Apr 2012 and Commons 2008.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: RSAF T-33A 1510, c/n 580-1425 (ABPic 27 Apr 2012; aerialvisuals, outdoor at 24.75293 46.73781). First of two T-33s at the museum.

description: Identified by ABPic (25 Apr 2012) as an F-86H, c/n 191-926, painted 709; aviationmuseum.eu also lists F-86H 709. Second of two Sabres at the museum. description: RSAF Texan painted 206; ABPic (27 Apr 2012) calls it AT-6B, aerialvisuals lists an AT-6D and aviationmuseum.eu AT-6D 206. Second of two Texans; indoor. Sub-variant unresolved.

description: Temco T-35A Buckaroo, c/n TE-6024, painted 108, understood to be a composite of several airframes (ABPic 27 Apr 2012, photographer's note). aviationmuseum.eu lists it as 34470. Indoor.

description: Full-size replica of the Wapiti, the first warplane bought by King Abdulaziz (RSAF's first type), displayed in a dedicated Wapiti corner styled as an old military camp (Saudipedia; aviationmuseum.eu; aerialvisuals list). Replica, not an original airframe.
museum_name: Saqr Al-Jazira Royal Saudi Air Force Museum

description: Replica of the DH.9A, representing the first aircraft acquired by the Kingdom in the 1920s (aviationmuseum.eu, aerialvisuals list). Replica, not an original airframe.
